definitions.explanation: A film produced in Western countries (Europe, America, etc.), as distinguished from Japanese or Asian cinema. A broad classification used in Japanese film culture.

examples.japanese: {西洋映画|せいようえいが}が{好|す}きですか。
{昔|むかし}は{西洋映画|せいようえいが}のことを{洋画|ようが}と{呼|よ}んでいた。
examples.english: In the past, Western films were called yōga.

examples.japanese: この{映画館|えいがかん}では{西洋映画|せいようえいが}と{邦画|ほうが}の{両方|りょうほう}を{上映|じょうえい}している。
examples.english: This movie theater screens both Western films and Japanese films.

notes:
Composed of {西洋|せいよう} (the West/Western countries) and {映画|えいが} (movie). In everyday Japanese, {洋画|ようが} is the more common and concise term for Western films. {西洋映画|せいようえいが} is the fuller, more formal expression.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {西洋映画|せいようえいが}ファン: fan of Western movies
- {西洋映画|せいようえいが}の{名作|めいさく}: masterpiece of Western cinema
- {西洋映画|せいようえいが}を{観|み}る: to watch a Western movie

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {洋画|ようが}: Western film — the standard short form, much more common in casual speech
- {邦画|ほうが}: Japanese film — the counterpart category
- {外国映画|がいこくえいが}: foreign film — broader, includes Asian films too
